contentBlocks.text: Last week you explored world communities and culture, including Punjab. This week: learn to read a world map!

The world's land is divided into 7 large landmasses called continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. The world's water is divided into 5 oceans: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic. Look at a world map. Which continent do you live on? Name one ocean that touches that continent.
You just learned the 7 continents and 5 oceans! Tomorrow we'll find your community and Punjab on the map.

objectives: Identify which continent and ocean are closest to home
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's world-communities/Punjab work briefly.
2. Introduce the 7 continents and 5 oceans using a world map.
3. Have the child identify their own continent and a nearby ocean.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's locating-Punjab lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just naming and pointing to the child's own continent first, before requiring all 7
Ready for more: ask the child to name a continent they'd like to learn more about and why
A real world map or globe makes this lesson far more concrete than description alone
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a map-reading activity — check that the child correctly names their own continent and identifies at least one ocean that touches it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's Geography dimension (using maps to represent the world) at a Grade 3 level, opening this week's map-skills thread as a foundation for the course's world-communities focus.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question using a world map.

rows.problem: Which continent do you live on, and which ocean is closest to it?
